title: Update Sets

sections.heading: Key concepts
sections.content: An Update Set captures configuration changes (customizations: fields, forms, business rules, UI policies, etc.) made on an instance so they can be moved to another one (e.g. Dev → Test → Prod). You must set an Update Set as 'Current' before starting work, otherwise changes go into the Default set.

sections.heading: Lifecycle
sections.content: An Update Set moves through the states In Progress → Complete. Once marked Complete, it should no longer be modified. On the target instance, it is first Retrieved, then Previewed (to detect conflicts), then Committed to apply the changes.

sections.heading: Important limitations
sections.content: An Update Set captures CONFIGURATION changes, not business data (records created by users, such as the incidents themselves, are not included). Commit order matters if several Update Sets have dependencies on each other.

pieges: Believing an Update Set migrates data (records): it only migrates configuration/customization.
Forgetting to set the correct Update Set as 'Current' before starting a development, which pollutes the Default set.
Committing an Update Set without doing a Preview first, thereby missing conflicts ('collisions') with the target instance.
